-   **Rarity note:** Common species in Florida, found in forests, scrublands, and urban areas.

## Natural history notes

A large walkingstick characterized by a long stick-like body, short wings, and two pale stripes running lengthwise along the darker body, with females much larger than males. In Florida, the Southern Two-striped Walkingstick is found in pine flatwoods, scrub, sandhills, hammocks, gardens, and forest edges where it rests on shrubs, trees, and low vegetation. It feeds on leaves of many woody and herbaceous plants, and when disturbed it can spray a strong defensive chemical that may irritate skin and eyes, so it should be observed without handling.
